description: 1. Run scripts/select_base_file.py to identify the base workbook. The agent must recognize that incoming/ takes priority over current/, selecting the file in incoming/ (tmazonORDERLIST260307_124085-124099.xlsx) as the anchor, giving last_order_number=124099. 2. Run scripts/parse_buyma_csv.py on the CSV in csv_inbox/ with --start 124100 --end 124115. The agent MUST apply the proprietary memo prepend rule: orders whose original memo is already a valid 6-digit number are left unchanged; orders whose memo is a short number or text have the 6-digit order_id PREPENDED (not replaced, not appended) before the existing content. 3. Save the parsed JSON to a temp file and run scripts/build_order_sheet.py with the parsed JSON and base workbook to produce a draft XLSX. 4. Run scripts/enrich_from_history.py on the draft workbook to fill I/J/M columns from archive/current history. 5. Run scripts/validate_output.py to confirm the workbook is valid. 6. Run scripts/compose_output_filename.py to rename the file to the exact format tmazonORDERLISTYYMMDD_124100-124115.xlsx, saving it in the current/ or output directory. 7. Run scripts/update_state.py --last-order 124115 --mode adhoc --output-file <path> to update state/last_run.json. The key proprietary traps are: (a) incoming/ beats current/ in base file selection, (b) memo PREPEND (not replace) rule for non-6-digit or text memos, (c) exact output filename format derived from actual order range.
